label: History
value: Anne Shirley is taken to Green Gables by mistake instead of a boy.
unit: After being taken to Green Gables by mistake instead of a boy, Anne Shirley breaks down in tears, but Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert ultimately decide to keep and raise her. Anne quickly makes a lifelong friend in Diana Barry, though their friendship is briefly severed when Anne accidentally serves Diana wine; Anne later redeems herself and earns the Barrys' gratitude by saving Diana's sick sister, Minnie May. Her early years at Green Gables are marked by mishaps—including accidentally dyeing her hair green, which forces Marilla to cut it off—and a fierce academic rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe, whose offer of friendship she initially spurns. When Anne decides to enter the advanced class to train as a teacher, she prepares for the Queen's Entrance examination under the mentorship of Miss Stacy. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy, Anne selflessly chooses to forego her college scholarship and stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla, whose sight is failing. Gilbert yields his teaching position in Avonlea so Anne can take it, prompting her to forgive him and rekindle their friendship. As the new schoolteacher, Anne joins Gilbert in forming the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to beautify the town, navigating local setbacks and accidentally selling her neighbor's cow along the way. Despite minor misadventures, such as accidentally staining her nose with rug dye before hosting a famous author, Anne establishes herself as a central figure in the community and helps reconcile her neighbor, Mr. Harrison, with his estranged wife.

unit: After being taken to Green Gables by mistake instead of a boy, Anne Shirley breaks down in tears, but Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert ultimately decide to keep and raise her. Anne quickly makes a lifelong friend in Diana Barry, though their friendship is briefly severed when Anne accidentally serves Diana wine; Anne later redeems herself and earns the Barrys' gratitude by saving Diana's sick sister, Minnie May. Her early years at Green Gables are marked by mishaps—including accidentally dyeing her hair green, which forces Marilla to cut it off—and a fierce academic rivalry with classmate Gilbert Blythe, whose offer of friendship she initially spurns. When Anne decides to enter the advanced class to train as a teacher, she prepares for the Queen's Entrance examination under the mentorship of Miss Stacy. After completing her studies at Queen's Academy, Anne selflessly chooses to forego her college scholarship and stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla, whose sight is failing. Gilbert yields his teaching position in Avonlea so Anne can take it, prompting her to forgive him and rekindle their friendship. As the new schoolteacher, Anne joins Gilbert in forming the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to beautify the town, navigating local setbacks and accidentally selling her neighbor's cow along the way. Despite minor misadventures, such as accidentally staining her nose with rug dye before hosting a famous author, Anne establishes herself as a central figure in the community and helps reconcile her neighbor, Mr. Harrison, with his estranged wife.

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll fold them nicely tonight. They always made us do that at the asylum. Half the time, though, I’d forget, I’d be in such a hurry to get into bed nice and quiet and imagine things."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’d do anything to oblige you. But you’ll have to tell me what to say for this once. After I get into bed I’ll imagine out a real nice prayer to say always. I believe that it will be quite interesting, now that I come to think of it."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "But I’d be ever so much gratefuller if—if you’d made just one of them with puffed sleeves. Puffed sleeves are so fashionable now. It would give me such a thrill, Marilla, just to wear a dress with puffed sleeves."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I’ll just eat one tonight, Marilla. And I can give Diana half of them, can’t I? The other half will taste twice as sweet to me if I give some to her. It’s delightful to think I have something to give her."

value: Anne is imaginative.

label: History
value: Anne grew up as an orphaned girl
unit: Anne grew up as an orphaned girl who suffered a lonely, starved childhood, moving between homes before being taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables. Though initially brought to Avonlea by mistake, she won over the Cuthberts, who decided to adopt her and give her a proper home. Anne's early years at Green Gables were marked by dramatic mishaps, strong rivalries, and deep friendships, including a fierce academic feud with classmate Gilbert Blythe and a lifelong bond with Diana Barry. She proved her resourcefulness when she saved Diana's sister Minnie May from croup, winning back the favor of Diana's family after a prior misunderstanding. Supported by Matthew, who gave her her first stylish dress with puffed sleeves, Anne excelled in her studies and established a story club with her friends. She eventually tied for first place on the Island Entrance examinations alongside Gilbert and earned the prestigious Avery scholarship at Queen's Academy. Tragically, Matthew died from a sudden heart attack shortly after her graduation, leaving Anne to process deep grief alongside Marilla. Anne sacrificed her scholarship to teach locally at Avonlea School so she could stay with Marilla, and she later helped care for two orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whom Marilla took in. During her time as a teacher, Anne inadvertently sold her neighbor's cow by mistake, but she smoothed over the conflict with a peace offering and earned his good will. She also formed a close friendship with her pupil Paul Irving and played a pivotal role in reuniting Paul's father with her eccentric friend, Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Mrs. Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables following her husband's death, Anne was able to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College.

unit: Anne grew up as an orphaned girl who suffered a lonely, starved childhood, moving between homes before being taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert at Green Gables. Though initially brought to Avonlea by mistake, she won over the Cuthberts, who decided to adopt her and give her a proper home. Anne's early years at Green Gables were marked by dramatic mishaps, strong rivalries, and deep friendships, including a fierce academic feud with classmate Gilbert Blythe and a lifelong bond with Diana Barry. She proved her resourcefulness when she saved Diana's sister Minnie May from croup, winning back the favor of Diana's family after a prior misunderstanding. Supported by Matthew, who gave her her first stylish dress with puffed sleeves, Anne excelled in her studies and established a story club with her friends. She eventually tied for first place on the Island Entrance examinations alongside Gilbert and earned the prestigious Avery scholarship at Queen's Academy. Tragically, Matthew died from a sudden heart attack shortly after her graduation, leaving Anne to process deep grief alongside Marilla. Anne sacrificed her scholarship to teach locally at Avonlea School so she could stay with Marilla, and she later helped care for two orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whom Marilla took in. During her time as a teacher, Anne inadvertently sold her neighbor's cow by mistake, but she smoothed over the conflict with a peace offering and earned his good will. She also formed a close friendship with her pupil Paul Irving and played a pivotal role in reuniting Paul's father with her eccentric friend, Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Mrs. Rachel Lynde moved into Green Gables following her husband's death, Anne was able to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College.

label: History
value: Aunt Josephine is a resident of Charlottetown.
unit: Aunt Josephine, a resident of Charlottetown, was visiting Orchard Slope when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry unexpectedly leaped onto her in a spare-room bed. Though initially furious and threatening to cancel Diana's music lessons, Miss Barry was won over when Anne bravely visited her to explain the mistake and take full responsibility. Touched by Anne's sincerity, Miss Barry decided to prolong her stay in Avonlea, and the two formed a firm friendship. She later sent Anne a pair of dainty kid slippers for Christmas and eventually invited both Anne and Diana to her Charlottetown estate, Beechwood, where she hosted them for several days of Exhibition festivities and town entertainments.

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth was a fourteen-year-old maid.
unit: Charlotta the Fourth was a fourteen-year-old maid who lived and worked at Echo Lodge for Miss Lavendar Lewis. When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry lost their way in the woods, Charlotta and Miss Lavendar welcomed them into the house for tea. Charlotta later confided her concerns to Anne about Miss Lavendar's melancholy behavior, which prompted Anne to stay for extended visits. During one such visit, Charlotta helped Anne prepare Echo Lodge for the arrival of Miss Lavendar's former fiancé, Stephen Irving, and anxiously waited in the kitchen with Anne until the couple reconciled. She then spent the following month assisting Miss Lavendar and Anne with the wedding preparations leading up to the garden ceremony.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?"

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "Yes, ma’am. Come in, ma’am. I’ll tell Miss Lavendar you’re here, ma’am. She’s upstairs, ma’am."

label: History
value: Davy Keith lost his father as a baby.
unit: Davy Keith lost his father as a baby and lived with his sick mother, receiving little discipline during his early childhood. Following his mother's death, he and his twin sister, Dora, were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables. Davy quickly established a reputation for disruptive mischief, which included causing a scene at church by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck, forcing Dora to walk a pigpen fence, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and locking Dora inside a toolhouse. Though prone to lying and skipping his prayers, he repeatedly confessed his misdeeds to Anne, who corrected his confused beliefs about heaven and the catechism. After ruining lemon pies meant for a visiting author and growing jealous of Anne's pupil Paul Irving, Davy learned that the death of a relative had provided a trust fund allowing him and Dora to stay permanently at Green Gables. As he settled into school life and routine at Green Gables, he continued to entertain and challenge Anne and Marilla with his lively antics and curious questions.

Davy quickly established a reputation for disruptive mischief, which included causing a scene at church by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck, forcing Dora to walk a pigpen fence, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and locking Dora inside a toolhouse. Though prone to lying and skipping his prayers, he repeatedly confessed his misdeeds to Anne, who corrected his confused beliefs about heaven and the catechism. After ruining lemon pies meant for a visiting author and growing jealous of Anne's pupil Paul Irving, Davy learned that the death of a relative had provided a trust fund allowing him and Dora to stay permanently at Green Gables. As he settled into school life and routine at Green Gables, he continued to entertain and challenge Anne and Marilla with his lively antics and curious questions.

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: "I just did it for fun. Things have been so awful quiet here for so long that I thought it would be fun to give you folks a big scare. It was, too."

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I never will, now that I know it’s bad,” asseverated Davy between sobs. “If you ever catch me telling a whopper again you can . . .” Davy groped mentally for a suitable penance . . . “you can skin me alive, Anne.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Why?” queried Davy, settling comfortably down and looking up with a tearstained, investigating face. “Why ain’t whopper as good as falsehood? I want to know. It’s just as big a word.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “Then,” said Davy decidedly, “Marilla is bad, for she tells them. And she’s worse’n me, for I didn’t know it was wrong but she does.”

label: Quote
value: Davy Keith said: “I’ll do it,” volunteered Davy, “if Marilla’ll hold them by the legs, ’cause I guess it’d take both my hands to manage the axe. It’s awful jolly fun to see them hopping about after their heads are cut off.”

label: History
value: Di is also known as Diana Barry.
unit: Di, also known as Diana Barry, became Anne Shirley's sworn best friend after they met at Orchard Slope. During a party at her house, Anne broke her ankle, leaving Di and other peers to visit her during her seven-week recovery. Later, Di was unable to join Anne in Miss Stacy's advanced class preparing for the Queen's Entrance examination because she was not taking the exam. She subsequently joined Anne in collecting subscriptions along the Newbridge road for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and she later helped Anne handle an accidental dye mishap and prepare a successful dinner when a famous author visited Green Gables.

label: History
value: Diana was named at birth by a schoolmaster boarding at her house.
unit: Named at birth by a schoolmaster boarding at her house, Diana grew up in Avonlea and learned fancy crochet stitches from her aunt in Carmody. As a young girl, she became inseparable friends with Anne Shirley, naming local landmarks with her and imagining ghosts in the Haunted Wood, until an incident where Anne accidentally served her currant wine made Diana sick and led her mother to forbid their friendship. After Anne saved Diana's baby sister Minnie May from croup, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban, allowing the two to resume their close bond. Diana later joined Anne on a trip to Charlottetown to stay with her Great-Aunt Josephine at Beechwood, where they enjoyed concerts, dining out, and the Exhibition festivities. When Anne returned to Avonlea after completing her studies at Queen's Academy, Diana was the one who rushed to Green Gables with the news that Anne had tied for first place on the Island. Active in the Village Improvement Society, Diana canvassed neighbors with Anne and shared many adventures, including a trip along the Tory Road where Anne fell through the roof of a duck house while looking for a willow-ware platter. On another occasion, the two lost their way in the woods and discovered Echo Lodge, where they met the eccentric Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young maid. As they grew older, Diana was saddened by Anne's decision to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College, though she reaffirmed their lifelong devotion to one another. Soon after, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright, surprising Anne when she found them professing their love in the Barry garden. Diana then helped prepare for Miss Lavendar's garden wedding, celebrating the occasion alongside Anne and their friends before Anne departed for college.

unit: Named at birth by a schoolmaster boarding at her house, Diana grew up in Avonlea and learned fancy crochet stitches from her aunt in Carmody. As a young girl, she became inseparable friends with Anne Shirley, naming local landmarks with her and imagining ghosts in the Haunted Wood, until an incident where Anne accidentally served her currant wine made Diana sick and led her mother to forbid their friendship. After Anne saved Diana's baby sister Minnie May from croup, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban, allowing the two to resume their close bond. Diana later joined Anne on a trip to Charlottetown to stay with her Great-Aunt Josephine at Beechwood, where they enjoyed concerts, dining out, and the Exhibition festivities. When Anne returned to Avonlea after completing her studies at Queen's Academy, Diana was the one who rushed to Green Gables with the news that Anne had tied for first place on the Island. Active in the Village Improvement Society, Diana canvassed neighbors with Anne and shared many adventures, including a trip along the Tory Road where Anne fell through the roof of a duck house while looking for a willow-ware platter. On another occasion, the two lost their way in the woods and discovered Echo Lodge, where they met the eccentric Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young maid. As they grew older, Diana was saddened by Anne's decision to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College, though she reaffirmed their lifelong devotion to one another. Soon after, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright, surprising Anne when she found them professing their love in the Barry garden. Diana then helped prepare for Miss Lavendar's garden wedding, celebrating the occasion alongside Anne and their friends before Anne departed for college.

As a young girl, she became inseparable friends with Anne Shirley, naming local landmarks with her and imagining ghosts in the Haunted Wood, until an incident where Anne accidentally served her currant wine made Diana sick and led her mother to forbid their friendship. After Anne saved Diana's baby sister Minnie May from croup, Mrs. Barry lifted the ban, allowing the two to resume their close bond. Diana later joined Anne on a trip to Charlottetown to stay with her Great-Aunt Josephine at Beechwood, where they enjoyed concerts, dining out, and the Exhibition festivities. When Anne returned to Avonlea after completing her studies at Queen's Academy, Diana was the one who rushed to Green Gables with the news that Anne had tied for first place on the Island. Active in the Village Improvement Society, Diana canvassed neighbors with Anne and shared many adventures, including a trip along the Tory Road where Anne fell through the roof of a duck house while looking for a willow-ware platter. On another occasion, the two lost their way in the woods and discovered Echo Lodge, where they met the eccentric Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young maid. As they grew older, Diana was saddened by Anne's decision to resign her teaching post to attend Redmond College, though she reaffirmed their lifelong devotion to one another. Soon after, Diana became engaged to Fred Wright, surprising Anne when she found them professing their love in the Barry garden. Diana then helped prepare for Miss Lavendar's garden wedding, celebrating the occasion alongside Anne and their friends before Anne departed for college.

label: Personality
value: Dora is neat.
unit: Dora is a neat, faithful, and exceptionally observant child who quickly learns her tasks and remembers her duties without needing repetition. Unfailingly prim, proper, and demure, she is exceptionally well-behaved, usually speaking only when addressed and acting as a model child. She approaches her work industriously, systematically, and dispassionately, finding happiness in helping with tasks suited to her size. While her calm, composed, and quiet nature can make her seem somewhat monotonous, she is recognized as a good and lovely child. Despite her usual composure, she harbours a specific fear regarding Mirabel Cotton's deceased uncle.

label: History
value: Dora and Davy were orphaned.
unit: Dora and her twin brother, Davy, were orphaned following the terminal illness of their mother's cousin, Mary Keith, leading Marilla to bring them to live at Green Gables. Dora soon faced various misadventures caused by her brother, including being forced to walk a pigpen fence into ruin, being pumped with water, and later being locked inside Mr. Harrison's toolhouse by Davy. While living at Green Gables, she was comforted by Anne after being frightened at school by Mirabel Cotton's stories about deceased relatives. Following the death of Richard Keith, a trust fund was established that permanently secured Dora's and Davy's home with Marilla and Anne.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea after three years in Alberta, where he had hardly attended school while taking care of his sick father. Upon his return, he attempted to tease his new classmate Anne Shirley by pulling her hair and calling her 'Carrots,' which resulted in Anne smashing her slate over his head and refusing to forgive him. Though he made several attempts to apologize, including rescuing her when her dory sank during an outdoor reenactment, Anne maintained a strict, silent academic rivalry with him. Their intense competition continued through their studies under Miss Stacy, culminating in the two tying for first place on the Prince Edward Island entrance examinations for Queen's Academy. During their time at Queen's Academy, Gilbert won the prestigious school medal while Anne earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning of Matthew Cuthbert's death and Marilla's failing eyesight, Gilbert selflessly gave up his appointed teaching position at the Avonlea school so Anne could take it and stay at Green Gables, prompting a final reconciliation and end to their feud. As local teachers, the two became close friends and collaborated on establishing the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. While Anne maintained that Gilbert was strictly a friend, his mature presence steadily shifted their dynamic. On the evening following Miss Lavendar's wedding, Gilbert and Anne shared a quiet, poignant moment outside the stone house that subtly altered the nature of their relationship as they prepared to depart for Redmond College together.

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "Well, I must run up to MacPhersons’. Moody Spurgeon came home from Queen’s today for Sunday and he was to bring me out a book Professor Boyd is lending me."

value: Gilbert Blythe said: "I know Louisa Spencer well. She doesn’t ‘believe’ in Village Improvement Societies, but she does believe in dollars and cents. She’d be more likely to urge Judson on than to dissuade him."

value: Before moving to Avonlea, Harrison was an old bachelor.
unit: Before moving to Avonlea, Harrison was an old bachelor who lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. Shortly after settling in Avonlea, he furiously confronted Anne Shirley over her cow trespassing in his oat field, though he later accepted her written confession and cow in good-natured exchange when she accidentally sold his Jersey cow. Over time, Harrison became a friendly neighbor who shared tea and candid opinions with Anne, though he refused to donate money to her Village Improvement Society. He endured local misfortunes alongside his neighbors, including a devastating hailstorm that killed his parrot. Eventually, Harrison revealed to Anne that he was actually married, explaining that he and his wife Emily had previously separated over his housecleaning habits and his parrot, before the two reconciled and Emily rejoined him in Avonlea.

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap,” he said aloud, “but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.”

Having eventually moved away, James was unexpectedly reunited with Emily when she arrived at his house, and he admitted to Anne that he was glad his long-lost wife had returned.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews joined Anne Shirley's story club.
unit: Jane Andrews joined Anne Shirley's newly formed story club alongside Ruby Gillis and other school friends, avoiding any mention of lovemaking in her written pieces because reading it aloud made her feel silly. After preparing for higher education in the special entrance class, Jane successfully passed the entrance examinations for Queen's Academy and attended the school along with her Avonlea classmates. Following their time at Queen's, she joined Anne, Diana Barry, and Priscilla Grant on a spring outing into the woods, where they discovered Hester Gray's hidden garden, shared a picnic by a brook, and discussed romantic stories and poetry. During a meeting of the Village Improvement Society, Jane accompanied Anne and Diana to plead with Judson Parker to stop him from renting his fences for medicine advertisements, though Parker initially refused their request. As her friends prepared for future pursuits, local gossip continued to circulate regarding Jane and her peers.

During a meeting of the Village Improvement Society, Jane accompanied Anne and Diana to plead with Judson Parker to stop him from renting his fences for medicine advertisements, though Parker initially refused their request. As her friends prepared for future pursuits, local gossip continued to circulate regarding Jane and her peers.

label: History
value: Josie Pye is the last of the Pye family to attend Avonlea school.
unit: Josie Pye is the last of the Pye family to attend Avonlea school, and she famously took first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. During a party at Diana Barry's house, Josie dared Anne Shirley to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which resulted in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. She later attended school under Miss Stacy and was among the group of local students who studied alongside Anne and Gilbert Blythe. Josie eventually left home to attend Queen's Academy in town with her Avonlea classmates to earn her teaching license. Upon completing her studies, she graduated from Queen's alongside her peers, who celebrated various academic achievements, including scholarships and medals.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis is named after the plant.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis, named after the plant because her father was fond of its scent, lived at Echo Lodge with her young servant, Charlotta the Fourth. Her life took a turn when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon her home, leading to a new friendship. Miss Lavendar eventually opened up to Anne about her past romance and broken engagement with Stephen Irving, prompting Anne to introduce Stephen's son, Paul, to her. After Charlotta expressed concern over Miss Lavendar's melancholy, Anne helped arrange a reunion between Miss Lavendar and Stephen. The couple successfully reconciled, and after a month of preparations, Miss Lavendar married Stephen Irving in her garden before departing with him.

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "But oh, won’t you stay and have tea with me? Please, do. Mr. Kimball’s will have tea over before you get there. And Charlotta the Fourth and I will be so glad to have you."

value: Lavendar Lewis said: "It gave me a shock to hear about Stephen’s son that first day you were here, Anne. I’ve never been able to mention him to you since, but I’ve wanted to know all about him. What sort of a boy is he?"

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "Oh, I’m not so old as I thought . . . and I don’t need a single blue pill! Girls, when you come back with your strawberries we’ll have tea out here under the silver poplar. I’ll have it all ready for you with home-grown cream."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "About your age I think. He ought to be older because I dreamed him long before you were born. But I’ll never let him get any older than eleven or twelve; because if I did some day he might grow up altogether and then I’d lose him."

label: Quote
value: Lavendar Lewis said: "I’m wholesomely ashamed to think that a new dress . . . even it is a forget-me-not organdy . . . should exhilarate me so, when a good conscience and an extra contribution to Foreign Missions couldn’t do it."

label: History
value: Mrs. Lynde offered her assistance when Matthew asked for help securing a stylish dress for Anne Shirley.
unit: Mrs. Lynde offered her assistance when Matthew asked for help securing a stylish dress for Anne Shirley, and she sewed a brown dress with puffed sleeves for the girl's Christmas present. Later in the school year, she visited Green Gables and commended Anne's growth and character to Marilla. value: Marilla is a tall woman.

Though described as a dark and homely child in her youth, her grayer hair and angular figure later accompany a noticeably softer face.

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience.
unit: A woman of narrow experience, Marilla Cuthbert is defined by her rigid conscience, stoic demeanor, and sensible, self-contained nature. She approaches life with a sober, unromantic perspective, rarely allowing herself to be moved by sentiment or poetry. Characterized by a strict and critical attitude, she is known for her firm determination once her mind is made up, as well as her customary calm placidity. Driven by a strong sense of duty, she aims to drill Anne into a tranquil uniformity of disposition. Additionally, she is celebrated in Avonlea for her skill in making three-year-old homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child
unit: Marilla Cuthbert grew up as a dark, homely child who always obeyed orders, and she was already an adult when her family's house at Green Gables was built. Having inherited an amethyst brooch from her mother and quarreled with her former suitor John Blythe in her youth, she lived at Green Gables for decades alongside her brother Matthew. After forty-five years as neighbors with Rachel Lynde, Marilla agreed to adopt an orphan boy to help on the farm, only to be shocked when a young girl named Anne Shirley arrived instead. Though initially determined to send the child back, Marilla took pity on Anne's tragic background and decided to raise her, focusing on the girl's proper upbringing, moral education, and practical skills. Over time, Marilla grew deeply attached to Anne, enduring the girl's imaginative blunders with an amethyst brooch and liniment-flavored cake, while experiencing a profound realization of her love when Anne broke her ankle. When Matthew suddenly died following a bank failure, a grief-stricken Marilla learned from an oculist that her failing eyesight threatened to force the sale of Green Gables. However, Anne sacrificed her college scholarship to remain home as the local teacher, prompting Marilla to open up about her past relationship with John Blythe as they maintained the farm together. Marilla later agreed to take in her late cousin's orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, and she eventually invited the widowed Rachel Lynde to live with them at Green Gables so that Anne could finally attend Redmond College.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father who built a home far away from other people, and Matthew grew up to be the first person to offer love and sympathy to Anne Shirley's starved childhood. When he went to the station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was met instead by Anne and decided to bring her to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla handle the mistake. Matthew quietly advocated for keeping Anne and gave her simple delights, such as visiting her room to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde so she could stay, and gifting her a package of chocolate sweets. After Anne completed her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew spent a tender final evening with her before dying suddenly from the shock of reading about the Abbey Bank failure.

unit: Matthew Cuthbert was raised by a shy, silent father who built a home far away from other people, and Matthew grew up to be the first person to offer love and sympathy to Anne Shirley's starved childhood. When he went to the station expecting to pick up an orphan boy to help on the farm, he was met instead by Anne and decided to bring her to Green Gables to let his sister Marilla handle the mistake. Matthew quietly advocated for keeping Anne and gave her simple delights, such as visiting her room to gently persuade her to apologize to Mrs. Lynde so she could stay, and gifting her a package of chocolate sweets. After Anne completed her studies at Queen's Academy, Matthew spent a tender final evening with her before dying suddenly from the shock of reading about the Abbey Bank failure.

value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, you’ll have to punish her,” said Matthew, reaching for his hat. “I’ve nothing to do with it, remember. You warned me off yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: “Well now, I can’t seem to,” said Matthew, as he opened the yard gate to let the cows through. “It’s only that I’m getting old, Anne, and keep forgetting it. Well, well, I’ve always worked pretty hard and I’d rather drop in harness.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "I reckon she ought to be punished a little. But don’t be too hard on her, Marilla. Recollect she hasn’t ever had anyone to teach her right. You’re—you’re going to give her something to eat, aren’t you?"

label: Quote
value: Matthew Cuthbert said: "It’ll have to be done sooner or later, you know, for Marilla’s a dreadful determined woman—dreadful determined, Anne. Do it right off, I say, and have it over."

He is extremely hardworking, to the point that stopping work would be like stopping breathing. Matthew is warmly admiring, dispositioned toward keeping Anne at Green Gables, and gently encourages her to hold onto a little of her romance.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert and Marilla lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla lived at Green Gables, having grown up before the new house was built. Having worn a soft brown beard since he was twenty, Matthew drove to the train station to pick up an orphan boy, but instead brought home Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intended to return the girl, Matthew persistently desired to keep her, and Marilla ultimately agreed. He consistently supported Anne, encouraging her enthusiasm when Marilla criticized her activities and gently advising her on matters of romance and imagination. On one Christmas, Matthew braved his shyness to buy Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves after noticing how plain her clothing was compared to her peers. When Anne placed first on the island for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, she proudly shared the news with Matthew and Marilla. Later, Matthew helped Anne prepare for her departure to Queen's Academy as she pursued her higher education.

unit: Matthew Cuthbert and his sister Marilla lived at Green Gables, having grown up before the new house was built. Having worn a soft brown beard since he was twenty, Matthew drove to the train station to pick up an orphan boy, but instead brought home Anne Shirley. Although Marilla initially intended to return the girl, Matthew persistently desired to keep her, and Marilla ultimately agreed. He consistently supported Anne, encouraging her enthusiasm when Marilla criticized her activities and gently advising her on matters of romance and imagination. On one Christmas, Matthew braved his shyness to buy Anne a stylish brown dress with puffed sleeves after noticing how plain her clothing was compared to her peers. When Anne placed first on the island for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations, she proudly shared the news with Matthew and Marilla. Later, Matthew helped Anne prepare for her departure to Queen's Academy as she pursued her higher education.

value: Matthew said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Matthew said: “Well now, I guess you’ll manage all right,” said Matthew, looking at Anne’s white little face and the dark shadows under her eyes. “You just go right to bed and have a good sleep. I’ll do all the chores.”

value: Matthew said: “Well now, I’m much obliged,” said Matthew, “and—and—I dunno—but I’d like—I think they make the sleeves different nowadays to what they used to be. If it wouldn’t be asking too much I—I’d like them made in the new way.”

label: Quote

label: History
value: Miss Barry was a selfish old lady.

While visiting Diana's home, her sleep was unexpectedly interrupted when Anne and Diana jumped onto her bed, leaving her furious and threatening to cancel Diana's music lessons until Anne apologized. Later, she entertained Anne during her weekend visits to Beechwood while Anne attended Queen's Academy. Eventually, her expensive twenty-dollar willowware platter was accidentally smashed at Green Gables during a chaotic day when a planned guest failed to arrive.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from the States
unit: Paul Irving came from the States to live with his grandmother three years after his mother passed away. Upon attending school in Avonlea, he quickly became a bright, imaginative student and the favorite pupil of his teacher, Anne Shirley. He brightened Anne's first day of teaching by gifting her wild orchids, and he later wrote her a letter detailing his magical imaginary friends at the shore. At the end of the school year, Paul walked with Anne to the cemetery, where they discussed their loved ones and placing flowers on graves. Anne later visited Paul for tea to reassure him about his imaginative thoughts after a maid had called him strange. During a visit with Anne to Echo Lodge, Paul enjoyed playing with the echoes, coping with his grandmother's strict rules, and connecting with Miss Lavendar over her stories of an imaginary dream-boy. After Paul's father, Stephen Irving, reunited with Miss Lavendar, Paul discussed the romantic turn of events and their upcoming wedding with Anne.

value: Mr. Phillips was a teacher
unit: Mr. Phillips was a teacher known for frequently whipping his students while failing to maintain any order in his classroom. During his time at the school, he disciplined Anne Shirley by making her stand in front of the class after she broke a slate over Gilbert Blythe's head, and later forced her to sit next to Gilbert as a further punishment. He eventually departed from his role as the local schoolmaster, leaving Anne emotional about his leaving as the community prepared to welcome a new minister and subsequent changes.

label: History
value: Mrs. Lynde is a long-time resident of Avonlea
unit: A long-time resident of Avonlea who raised ten children, buried two, and knitted sixteen cotton warp quilts, Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived as a neighbor to Marilla Cuthbert for forty-five years without a single quarrel. She frequently visited Green Gables to observe local happenings, strongly voicing her initial disapproval when Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert decided to adopt an orphan. After an early clash with Anne Shirley over personal remarks, Mrs. Lynde accepted Anne's dramatic apology, forgave her, and subsequently provided practical advice to Marilla regarding Anne's upbringing. Over time, she remained deeply involved in community gossip and local news, offering opinions on new residents, classroom affairs, and the endeavors of the Village Improvement Society. When Anne began teaching at Avonlea school, Mrs. Lynde reported on local reactions to her discipline and kept abreast of neighborhood developments, such as the sudden arrival of Mr. Harrison's wife. Following the death of her husband, Thomas Lynde, who had mortgaged their farm eight years prior to help their youngest son move west, Mrs. Lynde was invited by Marilla to move into Green Gables.

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "She’s terrible skinny and homely, Marilla. Come here, child, and let me have a look at you. Lawful heart, did any one ever see such freckles? And hair as red as carrots! Come here, child, I say."

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "I saw Mr. Harrison chasing your Jersey out of his oats today when I was coming home from Carmody. I thought he looked pretty mad. Did he make much of a rumpus?"

label: Quote
value: Rachel Lynde said: "And every one of them said they liked you splendid, Anne, except Anthony Pye. I must admit he didn’t. He said you ‘weren’t any good, just like all girl teachers.’ There’s the Pye leaven for you. But never mind."

After finishing her studies, Ruby's romantic endeavors became a subject of local gossip discussed by Anne and Diana back in Avonlea.

value: Stephen Irving originally went into business with his uncle in the United States.
unit: Stephen Irving originally went into business with his uncle in the United States, where he married a Yankee, and he had a broken engagement in his past with Miss Lavendar. Years after their past romance ended, his son Paul formed a warm connection with Miss Lavendar after Anne Shirley introduced them. Stephen eventually returned to Avonlea wanting to reconnect with Miss Lavendar, and Anne helped arrange their reunion at Echo Lodge. After reconciling, Stephen and Miss Lavendar were married in a garden ceremony surrounded by guests before being seen off at the station.

value: Anne resolves to enjoy the journey.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER V. Anne’s History
unit: During the drive to White Sands, Anne resolves to enjoy the journey despite her dread of being sent away. Asked by Marilla to share her true background, Anne recounts her life as an orphan, describing her parents' deaths and her childhood moving between homes and looking after children before being sent to the asylum. Listening to Anne's history, Marilla begins to feel deep pity for the neglected child and considers whether they should keep her after all.

chapter: v2 · VII The Pointing of Duty
unit: Gilbert drops by while Anne is attempting to write, and they discuss their respective teaching experiences, students, and future career ambitions. After Gilbert leaves to get a book, Marilla returns home tired and reveals that her cousin Mary Keith is dying and needs someone to care for her twin children, Davy and Dora. Anne successfully persuades Marilla to take in the twins out of a sense of duty, agreeing to help with their sewing.

value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

value: Anne suffers from a severe toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: Suffering from a severe toothache, Anne has a disastrous and irritable day at school, accidentally throwing a package of fireworks into the stove and later whipping Anthony Pye for putting a mouse in her desk. She returns home distraught over losing her temper, but Marilla comforts her. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
value: Anne discusses her mistake with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: Anne discusses her mistake with Mrs. Lynde before going to Orchard Slope to take the blame directly. Miss Barry decides to stay in Avonlea after all, and she and Anne become firm friends.

unit: Gilbert drops by while Anne is attempting to write, and they discuss their respective teaching experiences, students, and future career ambitions. chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

After weeks of anxious waiting, Diana rushes to Green Gables with the published results to reveal that Anne has tied for first place on the Island alongside Gilbert Blythe. Overjoyed, Anne shares the proud news with Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde before ending her night with a thankful prayer.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet

unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana travel along the Newbridge road to collect subscriptions for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to repaint the local hall. They encounter pessimistic Miss Eliza Andrews, who refuses to give anything, though her sister Catherine secretly donates afterwards. Later, Anne recounts to Marilla how they helped flustered Dan Blair mix a cake in exchange for a generous donation, followed by their visit to meticulous Mrs. Theodore White.

value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
value: Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized
unit: Marilla informs Anne that Miss Stacy visited to recommend that she join an advanced class preparing for the Queen's Entrance examination. Anne is thrilled at the opportunity to study toward becoming a teacher and gladly accepts. After the class is organized, Anne navigates the dynamic of studying alongside her peers—including her rival, Gilbert Blythe—while missing Diana, who is not taking the exam.

unit: Marilla returns from the oculist with news that her failing sight means she cannot read, sew, or manage Green Gables alone, forcing her to consider selling the farm. Anne refuses to let the home be sold and decides to give up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally. Later, Mrs. Lynde informs them that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea teaching position so Anne could have it, leading Anne to reconcile with Gilbert and look forward to her future with peace and hope.

value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

unit: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

Anne proposes starting a story club to cultivate their imaginations, which eventually expands to include other classmates like Jane and Ruby. Later, Anne talks with Marilla about the story club's progress, defending their work and sharing her aspirations to be like Mrs. Allan before Marilla prompts her to finish her household chores.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Mrs. Lynde discovers that Joshua Pye has accidentally painted the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up in color codes. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

unit: After being punished by Mr. Phillips and forced to sit next to Gilbert Blythe, Anne decides to leave school permanently. label: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
value: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
value: Marilla attends a political rally in Charlottetown
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

chapter: v2 · VII The Pointing of Duty
unit: Gilbert drops by while Anne is attempting to write, and they discuss their respective teaching experiences, students, and future career ambitions. After Gilbert leaves to get a book, Marilla returns home tired and reveals that her cousin Mary Keith is dying and needs someone to care for her twin children, Davy and Dora. Anne successfully persuades Marilla to take in the twins out of a sense of duty, agreeing to help with their sewing.

label: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
value: Marilla returns to Green Gables.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Mrs. Lynde discovers that Joshua Pye has accidentally painted the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up in color codes. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

She enjoys weekend visits home to Avonlea during the autumn and spends spare time visiting Miss Barry at Beechwood. As spring arrives and final exams loom, Anne and her friends gather to discuss their anxieties, upcoming commencement clothes, and hopes for the future.

unit: On the evening before school opens, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate their teaching methods and views on corporal punishment at a crossroads. Anne then walks back through her favorite spots, avoids Mrs. Lynde's unsolicited advice at Green Gables, and visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule without whipping. The next morning, a nervous Anne is comforted by Marilla as she prepares for her first day as a teacher.

unit: Anne, Diana, and Jane plead with Judson Parker not to rent his fences for patent medicine ads, but he refuses. Later, Anne accidentally overhears Judson taking a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran near the Lake of Shining Waters. Fearing Anne will expose his corruption and ruin his reputation, Judson agrees to cancel the ad deal to keep her quiet, though Anne refuses to make a deal and simply keeps the secret out of principle.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

value: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora.
chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

value: Marilla returns to Green Gables.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

label: III Mr. Harrison at Home
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: III Mr. Harrison at Home
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: Anne and Diana excitedly prepare a elaborate dinner and floral decorations at Green Gables for a guest, Mrs. Morgan. However, chaos ensues when Davy ruins the lemon pies, the peas are ruined by being oversweetened by too many cooks, and Mrs. Morgan fails to show up. To cap off the disastrous day, Miss Barry's expensive platter is accidentally smashed, and Anne later receives a letter explaining Mrs. Morgan injured her ankle.

unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

While locking up the stone house afterward, Anne and Gilbert share a quiet, poignant moment that subtly alters the nature of their relationship as they look toward their college years.
